title: Async tile rendering, legend skeletons, and screen-reader synthesis
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Background: Time-series dashboards increasingly render dense signals (tens of thousands of points across many series) for customers on both hosted and private deployments. Current monolithic paint and synchronous legend binding cause jank on lower-end machines and make keyboard/screen-reader interactions feel slow.

Goal: Design a non-blocking, tile-based rendering UX for large time-series that: 1) progressively paints visual tiles so core interactions (pan/zoom) remain responsive, 2) shows lightweight legend ‘skeletons’ while series metrics and color mapping resolve, and 3) surfaces an immediately useful screen-reader summary that incrementally refines as tiles finish.

Proposal summary:
- Tile rendering: split the visible time window into N horizontal tiles (adaptive by viewport width). Paint tiles asynchronously on web workers/offscreen canvas; commit to main canvas in ordered updates to avoid flicker. Prioritize tiles around the interaction focus (cursor/viewport center).
- Legend skeletons: show condensed legend placeholders with resolved color chips when available; defer long textual metric calculations (percentiles, uptime) and replace skeletons with full rows once computed. Provide an explicit ‘More details’ affordance for screen-reader users to request full metrics.
- Screen-reader synthesis: create an ARIA-live succinct summary immediately on view change (e.g., “Showing 4 series, center window: avg 12.3, peak 48.7”). As tiles finish, send brief updates that only announce significant deltas to avoid verbosity. Allow user preference to switch between ‘Immediate concise’ and ‘Verbose progressive’ modes in accessibility settings.

Design trade-offs:
- Complexity vs. payoff: off-main-thread tile rendering adds integration work with existing interaction code but reduces main-thread work and improves perceived performance.
- Announcement noise: frequent ARIA updates risk overwhelming assistive tech; we opt for delta-based announcements plus a user override.
- Visual consistency: skeletons must not cause layout shifts when full legend rows appear; use fixed-height skeleton rows and micro-transition animations.

Acceptance criteria (UX + measurable):
- Pan/zoom responsiveness: 95th percentile frame time for pan/zoom interactions reduced to <= 120ms on specified low-tier test device (Intel i5, integrated GPU).
- Progressive paint: first meaningful paint (skeletons + first central tile) <= 160ms after interaction.
- Accessibility: VoiceOver (macOS) and NVDA (Windows) announce initial concise summary under 250ms and subsequent delta announcements do not exceed one every 1.5s.
- Visual stability: no vertical layout shift when legend skeletons are replaced (CLS-like metric <= 0.02 on perf harness).

Deliverables:
- Design spec with tile sizing heuristics, skeleton row visuals, and ARIA announcement copy.
- Accessibility settings mock and keyboard flows.
- Handoff tokens for skeleton colors, animation durations, and legend row dimensions.

Notes on implementation constraints: Must coordinate with ENG runtime changes for offscreen canvas support and with ENG for batching and cache invalidation (tile boundaries must align with runtime caching to avoid redundant decoding).
updates: 2026-03-06 - Kickoff: aligned with Eng on worker/offscreen canvas feasibility. Eng noted CORS and image decoding constraints for offscreen; decided to prototype with transferable ImageBitmap approach.
2026-03-08 - Sketch review: PM and Research prefer concise default screen-reader mode. Decided to ship concise-first with opt-in verbose progressive mode.

2026-03-10 - Prototype review with Eng: agreed on tile heuristic (tileWidth = max(200px, viewportWidth / 6)); Eng will provide a metrics hook to report tile completion times. Action: ENG-4123 to add hook.

2026-03-12 - Accessibility audit session: voiceOver test showed repeated announcements during fast scrubs; adjusted plan to debounce delta announcements to 800ms and only announce when delta > 5% of avg value.
2026-03-14 - Handoff ready: design tokens and microcopy uploaded to Figma links above; PR referenced for runtime integration. Next: UX testing with selected customers and perf lab validation.
